results.market_title: Will OpenAI’s Astra model debut on the Arena Leaderboard at a score of at least 1510?
results.reasoning: Astra's public release has been delayed indefinitely after OpenAI's Aug 7, 2026 disclosure that internal evaluations could not rule out 'critical' cybersecurity capabilities, triggering a safety-driven slowdown with no new timeline given; release by the Dec 31, 2026 deadline is plausible but far from certain (comparable 'GPT-6/Astra released by year-end' markets sit near 60-70%). Even conditional on release, the Arena Elo leaderboard as of August 2026 already has the top model (Claude Opus 4.8) sitting right around the 1510 threshold, meaning Astra would need to debut as an outright new SOTA leader by a clear margin on first appearance—a historically uncommon outcome, as recent OpenAI flagship launches (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4) have debuted near but not decisively above the existing ceiling. Combining a moderate probability of on-time release with a low conditional probability of hitting such a high debut score yields a low overall probability, consistent with the crowd price.
results.key_findings: ["OpenAI disclosed Astra as its 'next major model' on Aug 1, 2026 via a math research post, with no model card, release date, or benchmark sheet (emergent.sh, mindstudio.ai)","On Aug 7, 2026 OpenAI announced it is deliberately slowing Astra's development after internal reviews could not rule out 'critical' cybersecurity capabilities under its Preparedness Framework, with no new timeline set (Axios, Roic News)","As of August 2026 the Arena text leaderboard's top model (Claude Opus 4.8) sits at roughly the 1510 'frontier' band, with GPT-5.5 Pro/Gemini 3.1 Pro near 1500, meaning the bar for a debut score ≥1510 is essentially matching or beating the current #1 model immediately (swfte.com leaderboard snapshot)","A related Polymarket market pricing Astra debuting at ≥1480 trades at 89%, while this ≥1510 threshold market trades near 10%, reflecting how steeply the probability drops as the bar approaches/exceeds the current leaderboard ceiling","Recent OpenAI flagship releases (GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5) have debuted competitive with but not decisively above the existing Arena leader, suggesting no strong base rate for a 'clear new #1 by wide margin' debut"]

results.market_title: Will Coco Gauff win the 2026 Women’s US Open?
results.reasoning: Coco Gauff enters the 2026 US Open as the #4 seed and #3-4 betting favorite (around +500, implying ~16-17% win probability) after winning the Cincinnati Open and having a strong overall 2026 season, but Aryna Sabalenka (two-time defending champion, ~23-24% implied) and Iga Swiatek are ahead of her as favorites. She has not yet played her first-round match (scheduled Tuesday Sep 1 vs Zeynep Sonmez) as of the data cutoff, and a deep, competitive draw including Sabalenka, Swiatek, Pegula, Osaka, and Andreeva makes a title far from certain. Multiple sportsbook and prediction-market sources converge on roughly 16% for Gauff, consistent with the crowd price.
results.key_findings: ["Sabalenka is favorite at +340 (~23-24% implied), Swiatek +480, Gauff +500 (~16-17% implied) per CBS Sports and legalsportsbetting.com odds boards","Gauff's win probability at Kalshi/DraftKings jumped from 11% to 16% after the draw was released (Yahoo Sports/Covers.com)","Gauff won the 2026 Cincinnati Open shortly before the US Open, showing strong recent form","Gauff previously won the 2023 US Open and 2025 Roland Garros, giving her Grand Slam pedigree, but was eliminated in the 4th round of the 2025 US Open by Naomi Osaka","As of Aug 31, 2026 the tournament had just started (first round Aug 30) and Gauff's opening match against Zeynep Sonmez was still upcoming"]
